$comment: Size budget for the Neyvia core installer, enforced by scripts/check_installer_size.mjs.
The core installer must stay thin: optional CLIs, models, GPU libraries, FFmpeg,
and marketplace applications are downloaded on demand and must never be bundled.
Budgets sit roughly 50% above the measured baseline so ordinary growth is fine
and an accidental heavy dependency fails the build loudly.
When a budget is raised, record why in this file's history — an unexplained
raise is how a thin installer quietly stops being thin.

measuredBaseline.note: First build that bundles the Python backend (grant_agent + runtime scripts).

history.reason: The desktop NSIS installer now includes the Python backend and its static configuration required for native chat. The prior resource-free installer could launch its web UI but left backend commands on an older per-user install. The 14 MiB NSIS limit covers this measured 12.84 MiB candidate with modest growth room; optional runtimes and models remain excluded.

forbiddenContent.reason: Node dependencies belong to the build, not the installed core.
FFmpeg is an optional media dependency, installed with the video module.
Model weights must never ship in the core installer.
GPU and ML runtimes are optional and installed on demand.
Mutable runtime state belongs in the per-user workspace, never in immutable installer resources.
Browser automation packages are optional; connected Chrome drives the installed browser.
